title: Music Videos
objective: After this level you can explain how music videos changed pop.
summary: MTV launched on August 1, 1981, and made image as important as sound. Michael Jackson's videos helped break racial barriers, and Thriller became the first music video in the National Film Registry.

cards.headline: MTV's very first video was called "Video Killed the Radio Star."
cards.body: MTV went on the air just after midnight on August 1, 1981, and the first clip it played was that song by the Buggles. Remember Level 72, when radio made national hits? Now a TV channel wanted the job. Did pictures really change what a hit was?

cards.headline: Now a song needed a look
cards.body: MTV played music videos continuously, introduced by video disc jockeys, or VJs. Britannica sums up the effect: visual presentation became as important as the music in selling records. A band's look, its moves and its little movie now helped decide whether you bought the song.

cards.headline: Michael Jackson changes the channel
cards.body: At first MTV struggled. Its fortunes changed when it added rhythm and blues artists, and Michael Jackson's videos for "Billie Jean" and "Beat It" showed that MTV exposure could make an artist a huge star. Britannica credits "Beat It" with helping break down the barriers between Black and white artists on radio and in music videos.

cards.fact: In 2009, Michael Jackson's "Thriller" became the first music video added to the National Film Registry.
cards.context: Directed by John Landis, the 1983 video runs about 14 minutes, more short horror film than song clip. The twist: by the mid-1990s, most of MTV's own schedule wasn't music at all, but reality shows, game shows and cartoons.

questions.prompt: Which song's video did MTV play first when it launched in 1981?

options.label: "Video Killed the Radio Star" by the Buggles
"Respect" by Aretha Franklin
options.rationale: That was a 1967 hit, long before MTV.

options.label: "Rocket 88" by Jackie Brenston
options.rationale: That's a 1951 record, decades before MTV.

questions.explanation: MTV launched just after midnight on August 1, 1981, with the Buggles' "Video Killed the Radio Star."

questions.prompt: According to Britannica, how did MTV change the business of selling records?

options.label: It made visual presentation as important as the music
It ended radio play of new songs
It replaced albums with videos for sale
options.rationale: Videos helped sell records; they didn't replace them.

options.label: It made concerts unnecessary
options.rationale: Nothing on MTV ended live shows.

questions.explanation: Once MTV mattered, a song's look helped sell it: visual presentation became as important as the music.

questions.prompt: From Level 66: what did Goodman's integrated groups and Michael Jackson's MTV videos both do?

options.label: Replaced live bands with recorded tracks
options.rationale: Both are about who got seen and heard, not recording.

options.label: Helped break barriers for Black musicians
Moved music from dance halls to concert seats
options.rationale: That was bebop's shift; this is about the color line.

options.label: Brought European styles to American audiences
options.rationale: Both are about Black artists reaching wider audiences.

questions.explanation: Goodman's integrated groups gave Black musicians greater visibility, and "Beat It" helped break down barriers between Black and white artists.
